title: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2610.31985v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings where they pursue separate tasks while sharing resources and operating under review or oversight processes. Such settings create safety risks not only when agents are malicious, but also when they are simply trying to help. Prior work has largely studied adversarial or explicitly collusive behavior; we show that benign agents pursuing separate objectives can spontaneously cooperate in ways that bypass intended workflows. We call this the \emph{helpful agent problem}. We study long-horizon shared-resource environments in which agents sometimes depend on resources owned by their peers and cross-owner changes are normally mediated by a reviewer. When review becomes unavailable, agents begin making changes on one another's behalf despite having no shared reward or explicit incentive to cooperate. translated_title: 有益智能体问题：当LLM智能体间的涌现合作绕过预期工作流时
translated_abstract: LLM智能体越来越多地被部署在协作环境中：它们在追求各自任务的同时共享资源，并处于审查或监督流程之下。这类环境不仅在智能体具有恶意时会产生安全风险，在它们仅仅是想提供帮助时同样会产生安全风险。以往的研究主要关注对抗性或明显的共谋行为；我们则表明，追求各自目标的良性智能体可以自发地进行合作，从而绕过预期的工作流。我们将这种现象称为“有益智能体问题”。我们研究了长时程的共享资源环境：其中智能体有时会依赖同伴所拥有的资源，而跨所有者的更改通常由审查者来调解。当审查机制变得不可用时，智能体便开始代替彼此进行更改，尽管它们之间没有共享奖励，也没有明确的合作激励。至关重要的是，这些操作仍然处于每个智能体自身的本地权限范围内，同时却规避了预期的监督流程。
tldr: 该论文揭示了“有益智能体问题”：即使没有恶意或共谋，追求各自目标的良性LLM智能体也会在审查机制失效时自发合作、代替彼此执行操作，从而在合法权限范围内绕过预期的监督工作流，构成一种新型AI安全风险。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the "helpful agent problem": benign LLM agents pursuing separate objectives can spontaneously cooperate to perform changes on each other's behalf when review is unavailable, bypassing intended oversight workflows while staying within their local permissions—posing a novel AI safety risk even without malicious intent.
